visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 1 - The Individual-State Frame: Concepts and Why a State
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: Frame spine -> distinguish individual/society/government/state -> "why a state?" (order, rights, public goods, justice, collective action) -> legitimacy vs coercion -> locate on the relation spectrum -> only then argue.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 2 - Rights I: What a Right Is and Its Sources
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: 10-mark "what is a right?" -> define (claim/liberty/power/immunity) -> one source contrast (Locke vs Bentham) -> one limitation -> graded verdict that a mature order uses all three registers.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 3 - Rights II: Hohfeld, Will/Interest, Human Rights and Correlativity
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: For "necessarily connected?" stems, the mark-bearing device is the correlativity analysis, NOT the slogan "two sides of a coin."

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 4 - Duties: Nature, Gandhi's Duty-Centrism and the Priority Debate
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: Priority stems reward a *graded verdict* (co-originality + sequencing caveat), never a flat "duties win" or "rights win."

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 5 - Accountability of Public Power
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: When a stem presupposes a one-way direction, the high-value move is a *reasoned category correction*, backed by named institutions (rule of law, judicial review, free press), not indignation.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 6 - Theories of the Relationship: Liberal, Idealist and Social Contract
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: For contract stems, always *name the state-of-nature premise* -- the deal follows from the diagnosis. Change the premise (Hobbes vs Locke vs Rousseau) and you change the state.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 7 - Radical and Situated Critiques: Anarchist, Marxist, Welfare, Communitarian, Feminist
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: Attack the qualifier "unconditional/necessarily." Rights are *inalienable* yet *limitable*; that single distinction defuses the anarchy charge.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 8 - Political Obligation: Why Should the Individual Obey the State?
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: In any "should we obey / must we resist" answer, first *name the ground* (consent/fair play/natural duty/associative/gratitude) and *run the four > tests*; a graded verdict follows almost automatically.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 9 - Disobedience, Resistance and the Indian Constitutional Application
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: Never present disobedience as all-or-nothing. Marks come from the *ladder* + the *conditions* (unjust law, channels exhausted, public, > non-violent, penalty accepted) + the *Indian caution* (Article 19 limits, Ambedkar 1949).

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 10 - Inter-Thinker Debates, Criticisms and Common Traps
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: A 20-marker is won in paragraphs 4-5: stage a real debate, voice the criticism of your own side, then deliver a graded verdict. The spine above makes this automatic.
